parts:
(this is probably mostly to Terrence again)

I have made progress!

I have 5 imputed datasets from mice.

The model converges without improper solutions for each run separately, with no warnings or errors. The summary() output is as expected.

Then I put the list of datasets into sem.mi(). No warnings or errors.

BUT: summary() of the lavaan.mi object outputs only coefficient estimates, no standard errors, fit statistics, or anything else, with no warnings or errors. 

fitted.cfa.mi <- sem.mi(lavcfasyntax, data=df.imputed)
(no warnings or errors)

summary(fitted.cfa.mi)
(no warnings or errors, but top of output below)

Development versions of both lavaan and semTools.

Help?

Thanks!

messages.subject: Re: Missing output in summary of lavaan.mi object
parts: BUT: summary() of the lavaan.mi object outputs only coefficient estimates, no standard errors, fit statistics, or anything else, with no warnings or errors.

What you are seeing is the summary() method for a class?lavaanList object, from which class?lavaan.mi inherits.  R is not finding the summary() method for lavaan.mi in your path for some reason (find many such messages on this forum about that).  What is your sessionInfo() output?  

Reinstallation helps sometimes.  I had to do this even for the CRAN version of semTools, when I updated R recently.
